newsitem.title: USA: Bank reform would eliminate federal thrift charter.
newsitem.headline: Bank reform would eliminate federal thrift charter.

text.p: In a bid to draw a final curtain on the savings and loan crisis of the 1980s, the House Banking Committee voted on Thursday in favor of eliminating the federal charter for thrift institutions.

In a third day of debate on legislation to overhaul aging U.S. financial laws, the committee rejected an amendment sponsored by Rep. John LaFalce, Democrat of New York, and Jack Metcalf, Republican of Washington, to preserve the thrift charter.
Provisions in the financial modernization legislation would force all thrifts to begin operating as banks, although with some grandfathering of their currently authorized powers.

In a vote that crossed party lines, the committee voted 26-23 to reject the amendment. The committee then went on to consider an amendment sponsored by Florida Republican Bill McCollum to lengthen the period under which thrifts would be allowed to operate under the grandfather provision.
The vote bolstered the chances for final passage of the legislation, because the banking industry has said it would actively oppose the bill if the thrift charter was preserved.

Bankers reluctantly backed the McCollum amendment. "It's not ideal for us, but we are willing to go along with it to defeat the (LaFalce) amendment," said Ed Yingling, the top lobbyist for the American Bankers Association.
